# Development Progression Report

**Generated by the Part 2 light-training script (Logistic Regression only, no
grid search, no CV).** Each stage builds on the previous one and is scored on
the SAME untouched held-out test set (NSL-KDD: 22,544 rows; CICIDS2017: 15,606
rows). The purpose is to show *which step of the pipeline moves the needle*.

## NSL-KDD

| Stage | What changed | Features | Train rows | Accuracy | F1 (macro) | AUC-ROC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Raw (no cleaning, no scaling, no SMOTE) | 122 | 125,973 | 0.6092 | 0.2738 | 0.6376 |
| **B** | + Preprocessing (impute, scale, encode) | 122 | 125,973 | 0.7512 | 0.5285 | 0.9267 |
| **C** | + Feature selection (consensus, 15 kept) | 15 | 125,973 | 0.6918 | 0.4325 | 0.8988 |
| **D** | + SMOTE (class balancing) | 122 | 125,973 | 0.7628 | 0.5572 | 0.9057 |
| **E** | + Grid-search tuning (saved model) | 122 | 125,973 | 0.7628 | 0.5572 | 0.9057 |

## CICIDS2017

| Stage | What changed | Features | Train rows | Accuracy | F1 (macro) | AUC-ROC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Raw (no cleaning, no scaling, no SMOTE) | 78 | 62,341 | 0.7834 | 0.6860 | 0.8798 |
| **B** | + Preprocessing (impute, scale, encode) | 78 | 62,422 | 0.9437 | 0.7888 | 0.9625 |
| **C** | + Feature selection (consensus, 7 kept) | 7 | 62,422 | 0.5638 | 0.3971 | 0.8241 |
| **D** | + SMOTE (class balancing) | 78 | 62,422 | 0.9364 | 0.7912 | 0.9795 |
| **E** | + Grid-search tuning (saved model) | 78 | 62,422 | 0.9549 | 0.8267 | 0.9784 |

## Reading the table

* **A → B (raw → preprocessed).** Jump from raw features to imputed/scaled/
  encoded features. For CICIDS2017 this step alone makes the model usable —
  the raw matrix still contains Infinity/NaN values and wildly different
  feature scales.
* **B → C (feature selection).** Restrict to the features all three selection
  methods (Pearson, mutual information, RFE) agree on. The consensus subsets
  are very aggressive (15 of 122 features for NSL-KDD, 7 of 78 for CICIDS2017)
  and — for Logistic Regression — they HURT (NSL F1 0.529 → 0.433, CICIDS
  0.789 → 0.397). The reason: LR already regularises away irrelevant features
  (`L2` penalty), and the strict consensus subset throws away correlated
  features that are still informative together. This is why the final pipeline
  keeps the full preprocessed set; feature selection is applied only to the
  tree-based models in the filter step of `src/data/feature_selection.py`.
* **C → D (SMOTE).** Class-balancing with synthetic rare-class rows (train
  only, inside the pipeline). Recovers all of the lost ground and then some —
  the effect is most visible on the classes that matter: rare attack recall.
* **D → E (tuning).** Grid-search hyperparameters. A real but small gain for
  CICIDS2017 (0.791 → 0.827 via `C=10`) and none for NSL-KDD (`C=1.0` already
  best) — a sign the pipeline steps, not the hyperparameters, do most of the
  work for this model.

## Source data

* `data/processed/development_progression.json` (machine-readable)
* Feature-selection consensus from `data/processed/*_feature_selection.csv`
